cards.explanation: The answer is True. Paul says it right up front: "See what large letters I am using to write to you with my own hand!" (Galatians 6:11). Paul, the apostle who wrote this letter, wants everyone to notice it. I think he's saying this one is personal, friends. When my stamp comes out in big, bold lines, I want somebody to notice too.

The answer is persecution for the cross of Christ. Paul says these people push circumcision "only" to avoid persecution for the cross of Christ (Galatians 6:12). They want to make a good impression outwardly, and the pressure lands on the Galatians. Persecution for the cross is the whole reason he gives.

The answer is False. Paul says, "For the circumcised do not even keep the law themselves…" (Galatians 6:13). The ones pushing circumcision aren't keeping the law. They still want it done to the Galatians. Paul notices that, friends, and now we all do.

The answer is flesh. Paul says they want the Galatians circumcised "…that they may boast in your flesh." (Galatians 6:13). The boasting is about what they can point to on the outside. I'd say that's a pretty empty trophy case.

The answer is the cross. Paul says, "But as for me, may I never boast, except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ…" (Galatians 6:14). He puts all his boasting in one place. I'd like to say I'm that disciplined, but I once bragged about a cookie for a whole afternoon.

The answer is that the world has been crucified to him and he to the world. Paul says the cross is the thing "…through which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world." (Galatians 6:14). It goes both ways. He doesn't explain it further in this verse, so I'll just let those words stand.

The answer is False. Paul says, "For neither circumcision nor uncircumcision means anything." (Galatians 6:15). He doesn't crown one side over the other, friends. Then he says what does count, and it's a new creation.

The answer is a new creation. Paul says, "What counts is a new creation." (Galatians 6:15). Circumcision and uncircumcision both get set aside. I was pulled out of a junk drawer and given a bakery, so a new creation sounds good to me.
The answer is peace and mercy. Paul writes, "Peace and mercy to all who walk by this rule…" (Galatians 6:16). It's a blessing for everyone who walks by it. Not a bad thing to have on a letter.

The answer is True. Paul gives that reason in the same breath: "From now on let no one cause me trouble, for I bear on my body the marks of Jesus." (Galatians 6:17). The text doesn't spell out what the marks are, so I won't guess. He just says he carries them.

The answer is the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ. Paul closes with, "The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers. Amen." (Galatians 6:18). It's a warm way to end a letter that had some hard words in it. I'd take that over a stern goodbye any day.
